description: Area Contingency Plans (ACPs) are the reference documents that US responders use for oil and hazardous substance discharges into navigable waters, prepared by area committees under Clean Water Act section 311(j)(4); the EPA page explains them and links the plans. Coverage: the Coast Guard leads planning in coastal zones and certain major inland water bodies and the EPA in inland zones, so the plans cover rivers, lakes and the pipelines, terminals and vessels that can spill into them. Each plan describes its area and its economically or environmentally sensitive places, assigns responsibilities to owners, operators and agencies, lists available response personnel, equipment and supplies and local scientific experts, and explains how it fits other plans, including the handling of recovered waste. Format and access: web pages and PDF plans, with links to the regional contingency plans of the 10 EPA regions, Alaska, the Caribbean and Oceania through the National Response Team. Licence and cost: free federal documents. Caveats: plans differ in detail and update date by region, and sensitive-area maps are not a uniform national layer. The listed resources, sensitive areas and responsibilities can configure emergency response and hazard exposure models of spills from inland waterway traffic and pipelines. It relates to the USCG National Response Center reports and the PHMSA pipeline incident data in the catalogue.
